items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I didn’t want to seem any less mature or knowledgeable than Leonard, whatever I was writing about.

ctx.x: Basically getting to know the whole scene as much as you can. I mean you said an important thing there, to write only what you know or feel strongly about.

Well I felt there was so much that I didn’t know anything about, and especially when I was 18 to 25 or something. I mean it was just scratching the surface. I had no idea what this world was that the music was coming out of. And I was interested but I wanted to be very respectful, I was a little shy as outsiders are. I felt like it was okay to ask questions, that’s the journalistic training I had. Ask a question. Find out. You are asking out of © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

curiosity. It’s genuine and it’s not displaying some sort of awkward egoness or even if it is so what. Nobody’s going to find that out on the page. Whatever the experience is when you do the interview, that’s not what you transmit to the page. You transmit to the page what you learned after the interview, what you’ve come out of it with.
